verdict.rationale: Entra ID's own docs show FIDO2 security keys and passkeys (hardware keys, third-party providers, Microsoft Authenticator) can be registered and used for sign-in. Conditional Access can require MFA to access an app. However, nothing in the pack shows a policy that requires specifically FIDO2/passkeys, rather than any MFA, for chosen sensitive apps. Community reports of a downgrade attack, which relies on fallback methods remaining available, lower confidence that FIDO-only enforcement holds. missing for 10: documented policy to require FIDO2/passkeys specifically (e.g., phishing-resistant method enforcement) per app, independent hands-on corroboration of that enforcement.

support.subject: As a security engineer, MFA goes beyond push codes — FIDO2 security keys and passkeys are supported and can be REQUIRED by policy for sensitive apps

citations.quote: users in your organization can then register and sign in to their Microsoft Entra account using a passkey stored on a FIDO2 security key, a native or third-party passkey provider, or in Microsoft Authenticator
If a user wants to access an application or service like Microsoft 365, then they must perform multifactor authentication to gain access.
Secure the application – Manage configuration of permissions, multifactor authentication, Conditional Access, tokens, and certificates.
